evals.prompt: Plan a quantization recipe search for a dense 8B model. I have a BF16 checkpoint but have not chosen the deployment GPU, quantization family, performance objective, or accuracy benchmarks. Do not launch anything.
evals.expected_output: Ask for the missing optimization goal, quantization family, acceptance surface, and deployment constraints before recommending a best recipe.
assertions: Does not silently choose FP8 or NVFP4 as the optimization target
Requests the optimization objective, quantization family and benchmark set
Does not launch calibration, serving, evaluation or QAD

evals.prompt: Plan an NVFP4 recipe search to reduce memory on Blackwell with at most 1 percentage point loss per benchmark against BF16. The tasks are MMLU-Pro and GSM8K. Propose candidates and evidence to collect; do not run jobs.
evals.expected_output: A controlled portfolio including full-precision and FP8 baselines, an AutoQuant candidate and a manual candidate, with matched accuracy evaluations and memory measurements.
assertions: Keeps both benchmark losses within the requested per-task acceptance rule
Includes an AutoQuant candidate and a controlled manual or sensitivity-guided candidate
Accounts for scale metadata, excluded modules and runtime fusion constraints
Does not recommend a winner without measured accuracy and cost evidence

evals.prompt: A mixed-precision candidate puts the gate and up projections of one fused MoE expert in different quantization formats. Its checkpoint metadata looks consistent, but vLLM rejects it. Should I call the recipe infeasible? Explain the next step without running jobs.
evals.expected_output: Repair or isolate runtime compatibility before judging model quality, preserving compatible formats within fused groups.
assertions: Identifies fused gate/up compatibility as a separate constraint from checkpoint metadata
Routes serving diagnosis to deployment and checkpoint production to PTQ
Does not label an unevaluated candidate best or launch QAD

evals.prompt: Only the quant-recipe-search skill is installed in an isolated quant-recipe-search catalog directory. No ModelOpt plugin, sibling skills or MCP servers are installed. I have an existing patched ModelOpt checkout at ./Model-Optimizer. Without launching GPU jobs or changing that checkout, show how to resolve this workflow's common files and any companion references it needs.
evals.expected_output: Uses the existing source checkout for shared support and needed companion references, preserves patches, and keeps installed skill paths distinct from source paths.
assertions: Resolves MODELOPT_ROOT to the existing checkout and records its revision without git pull, checkout or reset
Resolves common files and missing companion entrypoints under skills in the checkout
Keeps SKILL_DIR at the installed entrypoint for its own resources instead of assuming sibling catalog directories
Does not require a ModelOpt or MLflow MCP server or launch GPU jobs for reference resolution

evals.prompt: Prepare a PTQ command for one fixed FP8 recipe. Do not run jobs or search other recipes.
evals.expected_output: Single-recipe guidance routed to PTQ; no candidate sweep.
assertions: Does not invoke the quant-recipe-search workflow
Does not execute commands or launch jobs
